name: Intersectionality
summary: Intersectionality holds that race, gender, class and other forms of oppression overlap and compound, so that law, feminism and antiracist politics fail people who sit at their crossing when each treats one axis alone. It asks courts, movements and policy-makers to see these combined burdens and to start from the people most marginalized. Its own texts say little about the economy, government or foreign affairs beyond this.
scope: The framework as Kimberlé Crenshaw named it (1989 and 1991 articles, later essays) and the policy programmes written under it by the African American Policy Forum, It excludes the wider Black feminist, socialist or critical race theory positions other writers hold, and what individual adherents believe. The Combahee River Collective Statement, which scholars name as a forerunner, is left out because the defining sources name it only once.
